negativeResult.collection: Norwich city freemen register and enrolled apprentice-indenture index
limitations: Only enrolled indentures and admitted freedoms are captured; a Norwich youth trained by a master who never enrolled the indenture, or who never took up the city freedom, would not appear.
The only seventeenth-century Gurney is James, son of Francis of St Peter Parmentergate (bound 1627, freed 1648) - a Norwich-side witness supporting the two-Francis separation, not the emigrant John.

OCR and index coverage of the published registers is imperfect and the counts are a floor; a page-level scan of the emigrant admission window (c.1620-41, ff.170-180) is still outstanding as belt-and-braces confirmation.

finding.shortLabel: No John Gurney in the Norwich freemen or apprentice registers

sources.locator: Register of the Freemen of Norwich 1548-1713; Gurney entries ff.57b (1560/61, non appr.), 59b-59c (cordwainer dead by 1580), 181a (James Gurny freed 8 Jan 1648); no John Gurney freedom c.1615-1660
Index of Indentures of Norwich Apprentices, NRS 29; GURNEY, James, s. Francis of St Peter Permountergate, St Mich. 1627, 7 yrs, ref. E.17; no John Gurney apprentice enrolled

finding.statement: The Norwich city freemen register (Millican, 1548-1713) and the enrolled Norwich apprentice-indenture index (Rising & Millican, NRS 29) record no John Gurney freedom admission and no enrolled apprenticeship in the colonial-emigrant window, c.1615-1660. The registers' Gurney content is otherwise Elizabethan (a John Gurney freed not by apprenticeship in 1560/61; a John Gurney cordwainer dead by 1580) plus a single seventeenth-century entry - James Gurney, son of Francis of St Peter Parmentergate, bound at Michaelmas 1627 for seven years and admitted freeman under Henry Bond in January 1648 - which is a Norwich-side record of a Francis Gurney household, not the emigrant. The East Anglian formal trade-transmission pathway thus carries no record of John's training.
